analysis.evidence: וַיְהִי introduces the date. The clause חָרְבוּ הַמַּיִם then states what happened on that date: the waters dried up.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־

analysis.evidence: In בְּאַחַת וְשֵׁשׁ מֵאוֹת שָׁנָה, אַחַת supplies the one added to six hundred and agrees with feminine שָׁנָה ‘year’. The full date expression identifies year 601.
analysis.gloss: one (in ‘the six hundred and first year’)
analysis.morphology: Preposition בְּ ‘in’ prefixed to אַחַת, the feminine singular absolute cardinal numeral.

analysis.evidence: שֵׁשׁ counts מֵאוֹת ‘hundreds’. The conjunction joins בְּאַחַת ‘in one’ to שֵׁשׁ מֵאוֹת ‘six hundred’, dating the event to the 601st year.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וְ prefixed to a feminine singular absolute cardinal numeral.
analysis.sense: six as the multiplier in six hundred

analysis.evidence: שֵׁשׁ מֵאוֹת means “six hundred.” With אַחַת “one” and שָׁנָה “year,” the full expression dates the event to the 601st year.
analysis.morphology: Cardinal numeral, feminine plural absolute, with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: hundreds (plural מֵאוֹת, with the digits: three hundred to nine hundred)

analysis.evidence: בְּאַחַת וְשֵׁשׁ מֵאוֹת שָׁנָה means “in the six hundred and first year.” Genesis 7:11 explicitly counts the preceding year as the six hundredth of Noah’s life. Here the first month and its first day locate the drying of the waters within his next year.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, feminine singular absolute, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: The date moves from year to month to day. בָּרִאשׁוֹן gives the month’s ordinal, and the following בְּאֶחָד לַחֹדֶשׁ, “on the first day of the month,” supplies the understood noun חֹדֶשׁ.
analysis.morphology: Preposition בְּ with the definite article prefixed to a masculine singular absolute ordinal adjective used substantivally.

analysis.evidence: בָּרִאשׁוֹן identifies the first month. The following בְּאֶחָד לַחֹדֶשׁ specifies the day within it, “on the first day of the month,” with יוֹם “day” understood.
analysis.morphology: Prefixed preposition בְּ “on” + cardinal numeral, masculine singular absolute, used ordinally.
analysis.sense: first (in a count, and of dates)

analysis.evidence: בָּרִאשׁוֹן identifies the first month, and בְּאֶחָד לַחֹדֶשׁ gives the day within it, “on the first day of the month.”
analysis.morphology: Preposition לְ with the definite article, prefixed to a masculine singular absolute noun.

analysis.evidence: חָרְבוּ agrees with its plural subject הַמַּיִם, “the waters.” The phrase מֵעַל הָאָרֶץ specifies where the waters had dried up, “from the surface of the earth.”
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person common plural

analysis.evidence: In חָרְבוּ הַמַּיִם מֵעַל הָאָרֶץ, עַל locates the waters upon the earth, and מֵ־ marks the surface from which they dried up. The later phrase חָרְבוּ פְּנֵי הָאֲדָמָה confirms that the ground’s surface was dry.
analysis.morphology: Preposition עַל with prefixed מִן in the form מֵ־.

analysis.evidence: מֵעַל הָאָרֶץ locates the waters above the ground from which they had dried up. The repeated verb חָרְבוּ links this report to what Noah sees later in the verse: פְּנֵי הָאֲדָמָה, the surface of the ground, had dried.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הָ־ + common noun, singular absolute, common gender.

analysis.evidence: נֹחַ is the subject, and אֶת marks מִכְסֵה הַתֵּבָה as the direct object. Noah removed the covering of the ark.
analysis.morphology: Hiphil wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, prefixed with וַ־.

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for נֹחַ linked to the root article nuach.
draft.definition: Noah, the son whom Lamech names in hope of relief from toil.
draft.evidence: Genesis 5:29 gives the name נֹחַ and explains it through the wordplay on יְנַחֲמֵנוּ, “he will comfort us.”

analysis.evidence: In וַיָּסַר נֹחַ אֶת מִכְסֵה הַתֵּבָה, נֹחַ is the subject of וַיָּסַר. Noah removes the covering of the ark.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular proper noun without prefix or suffix

analysis.evidence: In וַיָּסַר נֹחַ אֶת מִכְסֵה הַתֵּבָה, Noah removed the covering of the ark. אֶת introduces מִכְסֵה הַתֵּבָה as the direct object of וַיָּסַר. The article on הַתֵּבָה makes the whole construct phrase definite.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected direct-object particle without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: מִכְסֵה is in construct with הַתֵּבָה, yielding “the covering of the ark.” אֶת marks the whole phrase as the object of וַיָּסַר (“he removed”). Noah removed the covering and saw that the ground was dry.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular construct, without prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Add תֵּבָה under its own consonants תבה for the ark in the flood narrative and the papyrus basket in Exodus.
draft.definition: An enclosed vessel that holds people or animals on the water, here Noah’s ark.
draft.evidence: Genesis 7:17 describes the waters lifting the ark. Genesis 8:13 identifies it as the vessel whose covering Noah removes.

analysis.evidence: In מִכְסֵה הַתֵּבָה, “the covering of the ark,” מִכְסֵה is the construct noun. הַתֵּבָה identifies the vessel whose covering Noah removes before he looks out and sees the dry ground.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הַ־ prefixed to a feminine singular absolute common noun.
analysis.sense: The vessel that carried Noah through the flood.

analysis.evidence: After Noah removed the ark’s cover, וְהִנֵּה introduces what he saw: the surface of the ground had dried.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־
analysis.sense: see or perceive that something is so

analysis.evidence: After וַיַּרְא (“he looked”), וְהִנֵּה introduces what Noah saw: חָרְבוּ פְּנֵי הָאֲדָמָה (“the surface of the ground had dried”).
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וְ prefixed to the presentative particle הִנֵּה.
analysis.sense: and there was (what one sees or finds)

analysis.evidence: When Noah removes the ark’s covering, he sees that the surface of the ground has dried. The plural verb חָרְבוּ agrees with פְּנֵי, the plural head of פְּנֵי הָאֲדָמָה (“the surface of the ground”).
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person common plural

analysis.evidence: פְּנֵי הָאֲדָמָה means “the surface of the ground.” The plural verb חָרְבוּ agrees with פְּנֵי and describes what Noah saw when he removed the ark’s covering: the ground’s surface had dried.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, common gender, plural construct, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: Noah looks out and sees that פְּנֵי הָאֲדָמָה, “the surface of the ground,” has dried. The marked noun names the ground whose surface is visible.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הָ־ + feminine singular common noun in the absolute state.
analysis.sense: the ground underfoot; the face of the earth
